title: orchis incarnata var. lanceata
intro: Orchis incarnata var. lanceata, commonly known as Lady's-slipper orchid, is a plant species of the orchid family. It is a type of terrestrial orchid that grows in the wild, primarily in North America. The plant has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties, which can help to soothe wounds, reduce fever, and alleviate digestive issues. The bioactive constituents of Lady's-slipper orchid include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its therapeutic actions, such as antioxidant and antimicrobial activities.
